about: The alarm-state order rule (the version vector and the set of heads) and what hangs from it: written by libs/nspanel-sim/vm/test/alarm-merge.test.mjs from the reference implementation libs/nspanel-sim/vm/test/alarm-merge-ref.mjs, which also checks this file is current. The Berry port replays every section and must give the same answers. The format is documented in the header of the test.

records.name: the initial record of the house
an arm with a wide vector and two devices left out
a trigger, untrusted, from the last node
a disarm with only its own dot in the vector

invalid.name: the vector does not hold the record's own dot (2:15, 3 in the second counter)
a dot of node 0 and counter 1
a dot of node 0 and a large counter
a dot of node 2 and counter 0
a dot of node 15 and counter 0
the first dot of the first node (the vector holds 1:1)
the last dot of the last node (the vector holds 15:1048575)

merge.name: the same action in two timelines keeps the larger mark, the older timeline's
the same action with equal marks keeps the smaller timeline id
layer 1: what descends wins over a later mark and over the disarmed
layer 1: a copy that descends wins across timelines and with an untrusted mark
layer 1: a vector that has gone past the counter descends from it too (it does not need the dot itself)
layer 1: there is no window: an ancestor a million actions back is still seen
layer 1: a node's later action descends its earlier ones, whatever else its vector says
layer 1 is strict about the counter: a vector one short of it does not descend, and the clock decides
layer 2: inside one timeline the later mark wins (an arm after a disarm)
layer 2: ... and a disarm after an arm
layer 2: marks compare across the wrap of the counter
layer 2: a trigger after a disarm wins
layer 2: a trigger before a later disarm loses
layer 2, equal marks: nobody can say which is later, the disarmed wins
layer 2, equal marks: of two armed ones the more severe (away over home)
layer 2, equal marks: a trigger over an arm
layer 2, equal marks and severity: the larger dot, only to be the same everywhere
layer 3: different timelines, the disarmed wins whatever the marks
layer 3: different timelines, two armed ones: the more severe
layer 3: different timelines, same severity: the larger dot
layer 3: the same timeline but an untrusted mark is not placed: the disarmed wins over the later arm

epoch.name: the epoch is saved, counted from the saved one, and the timeline is the node's own
a flash that refuses the epoch: a random one for this life, the saved counter left alone, the trust bit cleared; the next boot counts from the saved one

timeline.name: the younger timeline adopts the older and its own record moves
the older node keeps its timeline
a record from a timeline that is over is not translated
the same timeline: a larger time is followed, nothing is translated
the same timeline: an hour ahead is not a drift and is not followed
equal ages: the smaller timeline id wins, so this side (the larger id) adopts
equal ages: and this side (the smaller id) keeps its own

heads.name: two concurrent copies are both kept, and the safe side shows the disarmed
a descendant replaces the head it descends from and leaves the other one (the finding F2 in three copies)
a copy that descends from every head leaves one head
the same action in two forms keeps the one in the older timeline, the larger mark
a later action of the same node is above the earlier one, whatever its vector says of the others
an ancestor of a head is not added back, and nothing changes
acting replaces the heads that were shown: the new record is the only head and its vector is the join of theirs

situations.title: a copy comes back from a power cut with an old 'disarmed'; the house was armed meanwhile
armed; in a split someone disarms on one side, nothing else
armed; one side disarms at 150; the other disarms at 160 and arms again at 240
armed; a node restarts with no clock, alone, and the owner disarms there; nothing else happens
as S4, but the rest of the house disarmed at 120 and armed again at 200; the owner at the lone node disarms at 250
a node whose clock is 10 minutes ahead arms; the owner, in contact, disarms two seconds later
a node whose clock is 10 minutes behind disarms an armed house
the whole house boots with no clock after a power cut; B boots later, hears A, which armed, and disarms
half the house loses power at 100 and returns at 300; the other half disarmed at 150 and armed again at 250
the half that came back is alone and the owner there DISARMS at 320; the other half disarmed at 150 and armed at 250
the half that came back is alone and disarms at 320 (a copy still showed armed); the other half had disarmed at 150 and ARMS at 350
as S11, but the lone node restarted again at 330 before meeting anyone: its disarm cannot be placed in time

cases.name: a command a moment old is taken
the window is closed at 3 s: 3000 ms old is taken
stuck in a TCP socket that closed 15 s late (U19): refused
a stamp a little ahead is the error of two relative clocks: taken
a stamp far ahead is refused
a replay INSIDE the window is not the window's business (the mesh counter stops it): taken
the stamp wraps in 497 days and the age is still right across it

scripts.name: a recorded retransmission after the owner restarted: refused while it listens, then in another timeline
an issuer that is not synced issues no stamp

reconcile.name: a trigger is repeated until the siren confirms, and only then applied
a bridge that is not synced holds: it sends nothing and applies nothing
a siren that never heard the disarm stops at its own time, and the trigger is not re-sounded
a restart forgets what the devices confirmed: the first pass asserts the target even when it is OFF (A01)

reach.name: one applied an older dot and one is not heard
no owners: nothing is out of reach

want.text: Disarmed here, 3 parts out of reach
Triggered here, 1 part out of reach
